mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and increasing present value of future cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points over one month signals deteriorating labor market conditions and imminent economic slowdown, triggering immediate negative equity market reactions as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 12-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative equity market reactions as investors anticipate reduced corporate revenue growth and earnings downgrades over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production signals manufacturing sector contraction and supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in reduced economic growth and inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines, or regime-specific Rank IC falls below 0.025.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales growth directly indicates robust consumer spending, which is a leading indicator of corporate revenue growth and profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 75th percentile, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 0.5 percentage points over one month signals imminent monetary policy tightening, causing immediate negative equity market reactions as investors anticipate higher discount rates and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 1 month, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 12-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deceleration in payroll growth and rising unemployment rate indicate a deteriorating labor market, triggering negative equity market reactions as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and potential economic contraction over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS growth decelerates and UNRATE rises, or interaction term coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-interest-rate regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in the federal funds rate signals the onset of monetary easing, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines from above 4.0%, or regime-specific Rank IC falls below 0.03.
